company.name: sweetgreen
company.oneLiner: sweetgreen runs restaurants serving salads, warm bowls, and plates, with ordering through its app, office batch delivery, and catering.
company.customers: Individual diners ordering in store, in the app, and online; office teams through Outpost; and groups from 10 to 10,000+ people through catering.

blueprint.headline: sweetgreen can hand back store manager hours spent on staff schedules, produce ordering, and catering quotes, and cut food waste across its restaurants, Outpost routes, and catering orders.

agents.name: Weekly Crew Schedule Draft
agents.role: Builds the next week's hourly crew schedule for each restaurant for the general manager to review.

value.today: The manager builds the week's schedule by hand in a spreadsheet or scheduling tool, matching availability, time-off requests, labor targets, and expected busy periods for in-store, app, Outpost, and catering orders.
value.sizing: Hours per schedule built by hand x restaurants x 52 weeks

agents.impact: Each manager stops spending an evening every week building the schedule and only fixes the draft.
agents.trigger: Every Thursday at 06:00 local for the following week
does: Pull the last several weeks of sales by channel (in store, app, online, Outpost, catering) from the POS export
Read crew availability, time-off requests, and scheduled catering orders
Draft shifts by station and hour within labor-budget and max-hours rules
Flag unfilled shifts and hand over a draft schedule per restaurant

humanGate.detail: The general manager approves every schedule before it is published or shared with crew; the agent only saves drafts.

agents.evidence: The profile shows orders in store, in the app, and online, plus Outpost batch delivery and catering, all of which change staffing needs by day.

agents.name: Daily Produce and Protein Order
agents.role: Drafts each restaurant's daily perishable order for the manager from sales trends and booked catering.

value.today: The manager counts stock and guesses the next orders for greens, grains, and proteins like Miso Glazed Salmon from memory and a supplier order sheet.
value.sizing: Weekly spoiled or discarded food cost per restaurant x restaurants x 52 weeks

agents.impact: Fewer cases of greens and salmon get thrown out, and fewer menu items sell out during the lunch rush.
agents.trigger: Every day at 05:00 local before the supplier order cutoff
does: Read yesterday's item sales for menu items such as Harvest Bowl and Kale Caesar from the POS export
Convert sales and booked Outpost and catering orders into ingredient needs using the recipe sheet
Subtract the latest inventory count and draft the order per supplier
Hand over an order list with changes versus last week highlighted

humanGate.detail: The manager approves each order before it goes to a supplier, and any order more than a set percentage above the recent average needs a second look.

agents.evidence: The menu includes Harvest Bowl, Kale Caesar, and Miso Glazed Salmon, which rely on fresh perishable ingredients, and Outpost and catering add booked volume.

agents.name: Catering Quote and Order Sheet
agents.role: Turns a catering request from 10 to 10,000+ guests into a priced quote and a prep sheet for the catering lead.

value.today: A catering manager reads each request, picks menu items by hand, calculates quantities and pricing in a spreadsheet, and emails back, often hours or days later.
value.sizing: Catering requests per month x share lost to slow replies x average order value x 12

agents.impact: Group buyers get a priced quote the same day they ask, so fewer orders go to a competitor who answered first.
agents.trigger: When a new catering request arrives
does: Read the request for headcount, date, dietary needs, and delivery location
Choose menu items and quantities for the group size and dietary mix
Price the order from the catering price list and draft the quote
Produce a prep and packing sheet for the nearest restaurant once the quote is accepted

humanGate.detail: The catering manager approves every quote before it is sent, and any order above a set headcount or with custom requests gets a manual review.

agents.evidence: The profile states catering serves groups from 10 to 10,000+ people.

agents.name: Outpost Batch Prep Plan
agents.role: Builds the daily prep and pack plan for Outpost office batch orders so each restaurant can stage them in order of delivery.

value.who: Restaurant general manager or kitchen lead
value.today: A lead reads the day's Outpost orders, adds up bowls and salads by hand, and decides pack order and start time on paper or a whiteboard.
value.sizing: Minutes per day spent planning Outpost batches x restaurants serving Outpost x days per week x 52 / 60

agents.impact: The kitchen gets a ready pack list with start times, so no one totals office orders by hand each morning.
agents.trigger: Every weekday at 07:00 local, and again when an Outpost order is changed
does: Read the day's Outpost orders by office and delivery window
Total items and modifications by recipe and packing group
Set prep start times working back from each delivery window
Hand over a pack list and timeline for each restaurant

humanGate.detail: The kitchen lead reviews the plan before the shift; the agent writes only an internal document and never changes customer orders.

agents.evidence: The profile says Outpost delivers batched orders to office teams.

firstBuild.why: It brings in money directly: faster quotes win more group orders, and it needs only a request inbox, a price list, and email drafts, with no write access to operational systems.
scope: Read incoming catering requests and extract headcount, date, location, and dietary needs
Load the current catering menu and price list from a spreadsheet
Draft a priced quote with menu choices for the catering manager to approve
Save drafts only, with no auto-send
Track quote turnaround time against the old process

blueprint.nonObvious: sweetgreen's Outpost and catering orders are booked ahead, so they are the one demand that can be known days early; feeding them into schedules and produce orders before the app and in-store forecast is the main way to cut waste and overtime.
caveats: Systems in use (POS, scheduling, ordering, inventory) were not shown; categories are assumed.
Restaurant count, staff size, catering price list, and Outpost volume were not visible.
Waste levels and order values are not on the site, so sizing formulas use the owner's own records.
Supplier ordering practices and Outpost fulfillment details were assumed from how restaurant chains typically run.
